title: Preface
summary: The partial document covers the annual technical review for Riverdale Bicycle Works for the year 2025. It includes sections on the company overview, manufacturing sites, model lineup for 2025, quality and recalls, financial summary, and research and outlook.

title: Company Overview
summary:
The main points covered in the partial document include:
- Company name and founding details: Riverdale Bicycle Works was founded in 1998 by Elena Marsh.
- Products and production: The company designs and assembles bicycle frames in aluminium and carbon fibre.
- Distribution: The company sells through 240 independent dealers in the United Kingdom and Ireland.
- Employee structure: As of the end of 2025, the company employed 214 people, with specific breakdowns in different departments.
- Production sites: The company operates in Leeds, UK, and has a second production site in Porto, Portugal.

title: Manufacturing Sites
summary: The partial document covers manufacturing operations at two plants: the Leeds plant and the Porto plant. The Leeds plant has two welding lines, one for aluminum city frames and another for gravel and touring frames, with a planned annual capacity of 38,000 frames and a 2025 output of 35,900 frames. The Porto plant, purchased in 2019, focuses on carbon lay-up and painting, with a planned capacity of 26,000 frames per year and current utilization at 71%. Both plants share a single quality laboratory established in 2022 that conducts fatigue tests on 40 samples per month.

title: Model Lineup 2025
summary: The partial document covers the model lineup for the 2025 season, including five models: Kestrel 700 (road), Harrier ST (gravel), Owl 26 (children), Peregrine E (electric), and Swift 3 (city). It provides details on the weight, price, and additional features of each model.

title: Quality and Recalls
summary: The partial document covers a product recall issued in 2025 due to a weld seam defect in Harrier ST front forks. The recall involved 4,200 forks from batch H-2417. The company implemented dealer replacement of the affected forks free of charge within six weeks. Supplier changes were made, and incoming inspections now include X-ray testing of fork crown batches.

title: Financial Summary
summary:
The main points covered in the partial document are:
- Revenue for 2025 was 12.4 million EUR, up 9 percent from 2024.
- Export sales made up 31 percent of revenue, with the top export markets being Germany, the Netherlands, and Ireland.
- Gross margin was 27 percent, an increase of 1 percent from the previous year, attributed to lower aluminium spot prices.
- Operating expenses increased by 4 percent.
- The company ended the year with a small operating profit of 0.4 million EUR.

title: Research and Outlook
summary: The document covers research and development activities of a carbon laboratory, including a collaboration with Trent University on flax fibre composites, daily commuting tests with test frames, and future plans for an electric cargo bike prototype named Mule 1, with a target payload of 180 kg, for potential series production in 2027.
